title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
layout_note: Three titled panels left to right without frames - (A) Single-Step, (B) Multi-Step, (C) Our Adaptive Approach; A and B each run a simple and a complex query; C routes three queries through a central classifier to three strategies on the right.
grouping: Panels are separated only by whitespace and bold '(A)/(B)/(C)' titles; inside each, a query box on the left and its outputs on the right; iterative outputs (Documents, (Intermediate) Answers) are enclosed in a thin black rectangle marked with a circular arrow and 'k times'.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles: query boxes with coloured outlines and tints (orange straightforward, green simple, blue complex), outputs as plain light-grey rounded boxes; a database-with-magnifier icon for retrieval; small cartoon icons (a frustrated person, a gear with a warning) for failure verdicts; the classifier is a tick-box-and-pointing-hand icon.
proposed_highlight: The paper's panel is last and widest, titled 'Our Adaptive Approach'; its classifier label is set on a yellow highlight, the same yellow highlight that marks 'Inaccurate' and 'Inefficient' under the baselines.
lesson: Show a router by keeping each input's colour on the line it travels: three tinted queries converge on one classifier, and three lines of the same colours fan out to the three strategies.
notes: Venue written as arXiv: the arXiv v2 first page states no venue; remembered venue NAACL 2024 (unverified). year = arXiv preprint year. Cartoon verdict icons and database icons are embedded raster images.

arrangement.units: three unframed panels titled (A), (B), (C) side by side, the paper's panel (C) last and widest; iterative outputs boxed in thin black rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example questions in colour-tinted rounded boxes headed by their complexity ('Simple Query:', 'Complex Query:', 'Straightforward Query:')
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; failures are marked by highlighted verdict words ('Inaccurate', 'Inefficient') with a cartoon icon under the baseline panels
arrangement.shared: the same simple and complex example questions recur in all three panels; the database icon is redrawn at each retrieval

taxonomy.task: open-domain question answering that routes each query to no-retrieval, single-step or multi-step retrieval by a complexity classifier

insights.structure: Two baseline panels and the paper's panel stand side by side, ours last; in ours a classifier sits in the middle between the queries on the left and the three strategies on the right.
insights.data: The inputs are real example questions, tinted by complexity; outputs are named grey boxes (Documents, Answer, (Intermediate) Answers).
insights.emphasis: The adaptive panel is the widest and the only one with coloured routing lines; 'Classifier' is highlighted in yellow.
insights.flow: Short straight arrows run from query to retrieval to outputs; in panel C orange, green and blue curves converge on the classifier and fan out to the strategy rows in the same colours.
insights.avoid: Yellow highlight marks both the baselines' failures and the paper's classifier, and the classifier itself is a small hand icon; give the new component a shape and size of its own.

core.what: single-step, multi-step and adaptive strategies drawn as three panels side by side, ours last, the same example queries reused in each

relations.form: three panels in a row, (A) single-step and (B) multi-step each with the simple and complex query, (C) the paper's adaptive panel last and widest
in panel C three tinted query boxes send orange, green and blue curves that converge on one classifier icon at the panel's centre
from the classifier three coloured lines fan out right to three rows: Answer only (orange), one retrieval then Documents/Answer (green), a k-times loop box (blue)
the multi-step strategy is a thin black box around Documents and (Intermediate) Answers with a curved arrow between them and a circular-arrow icon labelled 'k times' on its corner
a database-with-magnifier icon labelled 'Retrieval' on the arrow from each query to its documents

channels.colour: colour = query complexity (orange straightforward, green simple, blue complex) on the query boxes and on the routing lines that carry them; yellow highlight carries two meanings - failure verdicts ('Inaccurate', 'Inefficient') and the new 'Classifier'
channels.shape: tinted outlined boxes = input queries, plain grey rounded boxes = generated outputs, icons = retriever, classifier and verdicts
channels.line: black arrows = data flow in every panel; coloured curves in C = routing by complexity; a curved arrow inside a box = a repeated step
channels.frame: a thin black rectangle = one iterated unit (the k-times retrieval-answer loop)

quality.strengths: The comparison is geometry: baselines and ours side by side with the same quoted queries, ours last and widest. The router is drawn as convergence and fan-out with each query's colour kept on its route, so which query takes which path reads without labels. Lines are short; the k-times loop is a compact boxed cycle rather than an unrolled chain.
quality.weaknesses: Yellow highlight means both failure and novelty. The classifier, the paper's contribution, is a small icon smaller than the query boxes. Baseline verdicts lean on cartoon icons (a frustrated person, a warning gear). Panels are separated only by whitespace and the outputs in C are not aligned with those in A and B, so the rows do not line up across panels.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
